text:
jamie_sales: FYI customer in regulated sector wants a truly air-gapped POC. No outbound egress, physical media delivery only. They asked about monthly delta updates on USB with strict signing and chain-of-custody.

maria_se: Do we have an operator-free install path for that scenario? Some customers disallow cluster operators.

alex_infra: Yes — we have a tarball + systemd service flow for non-k8s installs and a containerd compose option. Feature parity is limited: autoscaling/autonomous KV cache refresh requires our operator/runtime hooks which won't work in operator-less mode.

sam_sols: Important to nail down: (1) update cadence (monthly deltas?), (2) max payload size per update (they said <=2GB), (3) rollback strategy and acceptance windows, (4) who's responsible for physical custody during transport.

jamie_sales: They prefer monthly deltas and insist on <2GB per USB. No cluster reprovisioning during upgrades (so no blue/green). Also zero phone-home telemetry — telemetry only via customer-initiated support uploads.

maria_se: Delta <2GB is feasible for configs and small binaries. Large quantized model shards are a problem (single shard can be 20+GB). We can do an initial full seed transfer (sneakernet) then smaller deltas afterward if they accept it. Need product confirmation on model diffing.

alex_infra: Confirming: we can produce binary diffs for code/config layers. For model weights, we can do chunked delta strategy only if model format supports patching. Otherwise, expect occasional full-model shipments. Suggest documenting a one-time full model transfer then monthly weight deltas where feasible.

security_bot: Security checklist items: provide SBOM (CycloneDX JSON), detached signatures (sha256 + detached sig), signed release manifest, and optionally reproducible build attestations. Recommend customer-side signing with FIPS HSM if required.

jamie_sales: Commercial ask: what's the extra cost vs standard self-hosted? Do we charge a packaging/signing fee, and how do we handle recurring update validation?

maria_se: Typical pricing: one-time sealed-media packaging & signing fee (ballpark $6k-$10k) to cover manual validation, signing, and test matrix. Then either (A) standard enterprise license + support retainer, or (B) managed sealed updates: monthly validation + shipping fee per update. Emergency patches outside agreed windows are billable.

sam_sols: Proposed two-track offer: (1) Self-serve: customer gets signed bundles and docs; they handle distribution. (2) Managed update service: we validate and sign monthly deltas, maintain custody metadata, and ship media. Include SLA tiers (standard vs accelerated emergency).

jamie_sales: They require FIPS 140-2 HSM signing. Can they perform signing on their side and provide us detached sigs we ingest?

alex_infra: Yes. We can deliver unsigned artifacts and a signing tool (small CLI) that runs in-customer connected to their HSM, producing detached sigs we accept. We'll verify signature fingerprint and ingest signed manifest into our release metadata. This avoids transferring private keys.

maria_se: Operational note: blocking for support — with no telemetry we lose remote diagnostics. Support loops will rely on customer-initiated support bundles and scheduled on-site access. That raises support effort and should be reflected in the retainer.

sam_sols: Chain-of-custody template (draft):
```
COC-ITEMS:
- release-manifest.json (sha256 + detached sig)
- sbom.cyclonedx.json
- usb-physical-manifest.pdf (printed + signer stamp)
- custody-log.csv (UTC,timestamp,signer,method)
- media-serial-number
```

security_bot: Recommend adding quarterly CVE snapshot and a signed attestation for each shipment for regulatory compliance. Customer's compliance team will likely ask.

jamie_sales: Actions: maria to draft SOW + pricing ranges today, alex to validate delta generation approach for their chosen quantized model and confirm full-seed size, sam to produce chain-of-custody and shipping template, security to draft HSM signing workflow notes. I'll share the SOW with the customer on Thursday. :thumbsup:
